rebuff

rih-BUFF · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Rebuff is a blunt, abrupt rejection of an offer, request, or suggestion.

When the neighborhood association asked to use the mall's parking lot for a weekend fundraiser, the property manager's rebuff came within the hour, with no explanation offered.

Worked Example

When the salesman asked for a follow-up meeting, the store owner gave him a flat rebuff, closing the door before he could finish his sentence.

A rebuff is sharp and final -- it's not a maybe or a gentle no, it's a blunt refusal that leaves no room for negotiation.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

snub: A snub is a deliberate, insulting rejection aimed at a person rather than at any request -- cold treatment meant to be felt, like leaving one name off an invitation list. A rebuff, by contrast, turns down something actually asked for: an offer, a request, a suggestion.

veto: A veto is a formal block by someone with the official power to stop a proposal -- a mayor killing a council bill. A rebuff needs no office or procedure; it is the blunt, personal slam of a door on an offer or request.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

acceptance: agreement to a request or offer

welcome: a warm, friendly reception

Where it sits · how harsh the rejection feels — refusal → rebuff → dismissal

refusal vs. rebuff: A plain refusal is just a no -- it doesn't necessarily carry the sharp, blunt edge of a rebuff.

dismissal vs. rebuff: A dismissal stings even more than a rebuff: a rebuff at least engages your request long enough to slam the door on it, while a dismissal waves the request away as not even worth answering.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — re-

prefix — re-: back (Latin/Italian re-)

root — -buff

root — -buff: a blow, a puff of air (Italian buffo)

Put it together

Put it together: Rebuff traces back to re- ('back') plus an old word for 'a puff or blow' -- picture pushing someone back with a sharp gust of air. A rebuff is exactly that: a blunt, forceful push-back against a request or offer.

Use the root in a new word: buffet

Use the root in a new word: buffet: Fierce winds buffeted the little sailboat with blow after blow all the way home.

Root Check

Word Choice

Rebuff usually describes the act of rejecting someone's offer or request in a specific moment -- 'met with a rebuff' -- rather than an ongoing attitude.
